# K14. fp8q: the FP8 current-scaling quantize of the FP8 attention's q|k|v and dO (CUDA)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `AK_FP8CS_AMAX=1` (config L32), `AK_FP8CS_CAST=4,1,4` (config L32), `AK_FP8CS_AMAX_CFG=4,1,4,4,0,8` (config L32), with N10's `AK_FP8CS=1` (config L32) · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image: the same source, binary (`7c5815e0`) and wiring module.

## In brief

Transformer Engine (TE) quantizes the FP8 attention's q|k|v to E4M3 and its output gradient dO to E5M2 with per-tensor
current scaling in four launches (zero an amax, amax = max |x|, scale, cast). K14 (`ak_l8b_fp8q`, CUDA) does the same
arithmetic in fewer: for dO a partial-maximum pass and a cast that reduces the partials; for q|k|v the scale from the
partial maxima the RoPE forward wrote (K2 eager; K4 under CUDA-graph capture, whose second pass casts), then the cast.
A maximum is exact and order-free, and scale, inverse scale and cast use TE's formula and conversions: the bytes are TE's.
**Result:** byte-identical to TE's quantize in the kits on this image and the first-call checks of all ten runs, and on
all four called paths in unit tests on L4 v2's image (package `firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)).

## What it replaces (Replaces)

- **TE's `Float8CurrentScalingQuantizer.quantize_impl`** (`transformer_engine/pytorch/tensor/float8_tensor.py`), which
  is `tex.quantize(tensor, self)` (`tex`: TE's C++ extension), for every tensor the gate admits: four launches
  (`pytorch/csrc/quantizer.cpp` L980-1033), listed under Equivalence.
- **dO** (E5M2): all four, by `amax_cast` (two launches).
- **The packed q|k|v buffer** (E4M3; one flat buffer holding q, k and v, from N1): K2's or K4's partial maxima replace
  the amax pass; K14 replaces the scale kernel and, in eager forwards, the cast (under capture the cast is K4's pass 2).
- **Not replaced:** any quantize the gate refuses (TE's code runs it), and the delayed-scaling quantizers of the
  attention's S and dP (another TE class, not patched). Training calls K14 at the q|k|v size and on dO (Evidence).

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**TE**, for a bf16 tensor x (file `common/recipe/current_scaling.cu` unless named; TE 2.20.0 at `131157b5`, read in dev
image 0929's copy: [Provenance](../KERNELS.md#provenance) says how the submitted image's TE differs). fp8_max, the largest
finite value, is 448 for E4M3 and 57,344 for E5M2 (`common/utils.cuh` L1031, L1037).

```
amax      = max_i |x_i|        zero_amax_kernel, then amax_kernel: atomic max of each block's largest |x| (L24-70)
scale     = compute_scale_from_amax(amax, fp8_max, force_pow_2_scales, amax_epsilon, FLT_MAX)     one thread (L267-275)
data_i    = fp8(x_i · scale)   the FP8 cast (nvte_quantize_v2): fp32 product, saturating conversion, round to nearest
scale_inv = __frcp_rn(scale)   the inverse scale, written by the cast's block 0 (reciprocal<float>, utils.cuh L945-951)
compute_scale_from_amax (common/recipe/recipe_common.cuh L14-49): if amax < epsilon: amax = epsilon
  scale = 1 if amax is Inf, 0 or NaN; else fp8_max / amax (__fdiv_rn: one correctly rounded division), FLT_MAX if Inf
  if force_pow_2_scales: clear the mantissa bits of scale (bits & 0xFF800000)
```

`force_pow_2_scales` and `amax_epsilon` are the quantizer's own settings (`quantizer.cpp` L1005-1006). The amax and the
scale live in a two-value buffer local to the call (`quantizer.cpp` L1035-1040): the stock quantize keeps no state.

**K14** (`ak_l8b_fp8q.cu`; its `compute_scale_from_amax`, L32-46, is TE's line for line; the wiring passes fp8_max
and the quantizer's own `force_pow_2_scales` and `amax_epsilon`, `ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L143-145):

```
amax_cast        pass 1: part[b] = max |x_i| over the elements block b reads              amax_part_kernel L67-89
                 pass 2, every block: amax = max_b part[b]
                                      scale = compute_scale_from_amax(amax, ..., FLT_MAX)  cast_kernel L120-129
                         block 0:     scale_inv = __frcp_rn(scale)
                         data_i = cvt_fp8(x_i · scale, saturating)                         cast8 L91-108
scale_from_partials(part)  one block of 1,024 threads: amax = max_p part[p]; scale; scale_inv   L152-168
cast_from_ws               data_i = cvt_fp8(x_i · ws[0], saturating), ws[0] the scale            L130-131, L257-267
```

**Why the bytes are equal.**
- **Amax.** |x| of a bf16 value is exact in fp32, and a maximum is exact and independent of order, so the maximum of
  partial maxima that together cover every element is TE's amax. No atomics; every partial starts at 0, as TE's zeroed
  amax; lanes past the end read zeros (L74, L82); `fmaxf` skips NaN (header L4); the byte tests include NaN and ±Inf.
- **Scale and `scale_inv`.** The same function and arguments, FLT_MAX for an infinite quotient (TE:
  `std::numeric_limits<float>::max()`, `current_scaling.cu` L274-275; K14: L124, L162); every cast block of `amax_cast`
  computes it from the same partials, so all use one value. `scale_inv` = `__frcp_rn(scale)` on both sides (L126, L164).
- **Cast.** fp32 product of the bf16 value and the scale, converted by `__nv_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2(…, __NV_SATFINITE, …)`
  (L102): TE's saturating round to nearest. Walk order and vectors per thread change which thread writes an element,
  not its value (header L12-15).
- **q|k|v.** `scale_from_partials` takes the maximum of K2's (eager) or K4's (captured) per-position partial maxima, each
  the largest |·| of the bf16 values the RoPE forward stores (K2) or would store (K4) at one (sequence, micro-batch)
  position; the positions cover the buffer once ([K2](K02_x12a_qkv_rope_amax.md), [K4](K04_qkvx_qkv_direct_rope_bwd.md)).
  Eager forwards then `cast_from_ws` the written buffer; under capture K4's pass 2 casts from the RoPE's inputs with
  K14's scale.
- **The output tensor** is what `tex.quantize` returns: TE's own `tex.create_empty_quantized_tensor` (the quantizer's
  C++ `create_tensor`) allocates it and K14 fills its FP8 data and `scale_inv`; row-wise only, so no transpose
  (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L140-157).

**Class E0:** byte-identical to the stock path on every tested input.

**State kept between calls** ([the index's table](../KERNELS.md#state-kept-between-calls-tr-83)). None in the kernel:
`amax_cast` allocates its partials and workspace per call (L221, L229); the other entry points write only the caller's
buffers. The wiring keeps the checked (path, shape, format) keys, call counters and the extension
(`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L35, L50-57), and uses the last packed q|k|v buffer's registration once, for the first eligible
quantize of a tensor with that pointer and element count (L73-84).
For QKV direct it also holds the RoPE's inputs, K4's passes and a flag that the QKV-direct check ran (L165-167,
L190-192). A buffer K4 left unwritten under capture raises if quantized outside capture (L201-217) or if the next packed
forward finds it unquantized (patch `te/0001` L83-84, L205-206, L230-231).

## Numerics (Numerics)

The recipe's per-tensor current scaling (Numerical formats (TR-5.2a)): q|k|v in E4M3, dO in E5M2, one fp32 scale per
tensor from its own amax, `scale_inv` stored with the FP8 data; bf16 input, fp32 product, one saturating
round-to-nearest conversion. S and dP keep TE's delayed scaling. As in TE, an amax of Inf or 0 gives scale 1, and one so
small that fp8_max / amax overflows gives FLT_MAX: K2's kit's tiny and subnormal inputs take this branch at four of its
five sizes (`scale_inv` 2.93874e-39 on both sides); at the dO size those two inputs give `scale_inv` 1 on both sides.

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

Not applicable: K14 quantizes attention inputs and dO; it touches no weight or optimizer state and computes no gradient
or norm.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **`_eligible`** (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L134-138): a plain `torch.Tensor` (not a subclass), CUDA, bf16, contiguous,
  non-empty, element count a multiple of 8, data pointer 16-byte aligned; a quantizer with row-wise usage on, column-wise
  off, no amax reduction across ranks (`with_amax_reduction`), format E4M3 or E5M2. Else TE's `quantize_impl` runs
  (L195-196). **The path:** the registered q|k|v buffer takes the partials path; any other admitted tensor the amax path
  when `AK_FP8CS_AMAX=1`, else TE's quantize (L197-201). A registered buffer that K4 left unwritten takes the QKV-direct
  form; outside capture it raises (L204-208).
- **In the kernel**, `check_io` (L170-178) and `scale_from_partials` (L272-274) raise unless the same tensor conditions
  hold and the outputs are valid: FP8 data contiguous uint8, the input's element count, 8-byte aligned; `scale_inv` fp32,
  at least one element; partials fp32, contiguous; a workspace of at least 3 values.
- **Shapes.** Any element count that is a multiple of 8; offsets are 64-bit (L72-77, L133-137), and the persistent grid
  is at most the SM count times the blocks per SM. Training sends two shapes: the q|k|v buffer, 100,663,296 bf16
  elements (E4M3), and dO, [8192, 2, 32, 128] (E5M2) (`result_1.txt` L869, L899). Any other admitted
  shape runs the same kernels, and its first eager call is compared with TE (Enablement).

### Assumptions not checked in code

1. **The registration identifies the buffer by data pointer and element count only** (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L80).
   K14 takes the registered partial maxima as the amax of that tensor's current contents. This assumes nothing writes
   the buffer between the RoPE forward and its quantize, no other tensor with the same address and size is quantized
   first, and the partials cover every element (one per position: K2, K4); nothing compares their number with the
   tensor. If any of this failed, the scale would be wrong: **SILENT**. What keeps it true: in training N1 quantizes the
   buffer through a zero-copy view of the same storage right after the forward (N1, K2), and the first eager call is
   compared with TE.
2. **Under capture the bf16 q|k|v buffer is never written** (K4's form): K14's scale and K4's pass 2 produce the FP8
   bytes. This relies on the quantize being the buffer's only reader, an assumption of K4 and N10 (K4, "Assumptions not
   checked in code"). If something else read the buffer, it would read unwritten memory: **SILENT**.

### Benchmark detection

The gate tests the tensor's type, dtype, layout, alignment and the quantizer's settings; the kernels take the element
count from the call, with no shape constant, and the launch shapes are switches. K14 does not detect the benchmark
(Benchmark detection is not allowed, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switches** (config L32, read at `import firmus_ak`): `AK_FP8CS` (N10's) arms the patch;
  `AK_FP8CS_AMAX` adds the amax path (without it only the registered q|k|v buffer uses K14); `AK_FP8CS_CAST`
  (`cast_from_ws`) and `AK_FP8CS_AMAX_CFG` (`amax_cast`: amax pass, then cast) set vectors per thread, walk back to front
  (1) or front to back (0), and blocks per SM. Code defaults (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py`): on/off switches off (`"0"`, L34,
  L37), launch shapes the leaf's values (L38-39); an assertion requires 3 and 6 integers (L40). A vector is 16 bytes (8
  bf16 values); 4, 2 and 1 vectors per thread (any other value selects 1) and both walk directions are compiled
  (L192-201, L224-226). Unselected variants never run; K2's kit compares those of `amax_cast` with TE.
- **Import.** The extension is imported at the first eligible quantize from `AK_FP8CS_EXT_DIR=/opt/firmus/ak/lib`, set
  by the image and the module's default (Dockerfile L137; `ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L52); a failed import raises there,
  with no fallback. The integrity check at `import firmus_ak` re-hashes `lib/ak_l8b_fp8q.so` with the
  rest of the build record ([the index](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).
- **First-call checks.** For each (path, shape, format), the first call outside capture also runs TE's own
  `quantize_impl` on the same tensor and compares FP8 data, `scale_inv`, transpose and result type as bytes
  (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L209-232, L236); every rank raises on a mismatch, and rank 0 prints the verdict in its ARMED
  line (printed when a replacement arms). Later calls of a checked key and every call under capture (L210-211) run
  without a comparison.
- **The QKV-direct check** runs once per process, at the first eager quantize of a registered buffer: K4's pass 1,
  K14's `scale_from_partials` and K4's pass 2 into scratch buffers, then the amax against the largest of K2's partial
  maxima and the FP8 data and `scale_inv` against TE's quantize of the written buffer (the partial maxima themselves are
  reported, not required). Only after it passes may a captured forward leave the buffer unwritten
  (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L165-192, L211, L233-234; patch `te/0001` L215). So the captured q|k|v form, which every
  timed step runs, is checked once per run, at the first eager quantize.
- **Run-start gate.** fp8cs's row passes once at least one path has been checked (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L50-52; True in `result_1.txt` L946, one of the 19 armed parts the gate lists).
  Its verdict is per rank: each rank checks its own parts and raises if one has not completed its check
  ([the index](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).

## Approval (Approval)

None needed. K14 is E0 and keeps the recipe's FP8 formats and scaling; Graph Execution (TR-8.3) allows mathematically
equivalent changes to the non-weight parts of the computation. Only the number of launches and memory traffic change.

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: on this image the kits of K14 and K2 find K14's bytes equal to TE's quantize, and
the four first-call checks are True in the smoke run and all ten scored runs; the unit tests of all four called paths
ran on L4 v2's image (below).

### Tests on the submitted image

The kits below are among the 24 re-targeted kits run on this image's installed files, 48 / 48 PASS (R1, R3).

- **The kit for this kernel, PASS in both forms** (R1): as written, and with the allocator cache first filled with
  random bytes. The kit (this kernel's frozen development tests, re-targeted at the image) loads the image's binary
  (`7c5815e0`), K2's and K3's files and the installed TE files; one test measures time only. The wiring self-test (R2)
  arms a kit-carried earlier N10 module (`bca2c940`, not the image's `1aca679a`) and K1 file (`a91b35c1`). Eagerly it
  compares K14's three paths with TE's quantize (partials E4M3; amax E4M3 at the q|k|v size; amax E5M2 on dO): all
  True. Its QKV-direct line runs K3's Triton pass (`fused_qkv_rope_fp8.py` `8d378708`; `AK_QKV_DIRECT_IMPL` unset),
  which training never runs, with K14's scale. Under CUDA graphs, captures with the direct form on and off replayed the
  eager, TE-checked forward's FP8 bytes and `scale_inv`, and a captured dO quantize replayed TE's eager bytes.
- **K2's kit tests this binary directly, PASS in both forms** (R3). Its FP8 cast test compares K14's amax path with
  TE's quantize (FP8 data, `scale_inv`, type): 35 checks, five sizes (the q|k|v size in E4M3, dO in E5M2, 8,000,024
  elements in E5M2, 40 and 32,776 in E4M3) × seven kinds of data (Gaussian, zeros, tiny ×1e-38, Inf, NaN at every
  9,973rd element, ±3e38, subnormal ×1e-39), each in five launch variants. The same inputs go through the partials path
  (`scale_from_partials`, `cast_from_ws`) in four launch orders, and three q|k|v casts from K2's partial maxima are
  compared with TE's quantize. The log prints each input's first amax-path variant; the other variants and the partials
  path on the 35 inputs print only on a mismatch, and the failure count covers all: `FAILURES 0`, in both forms.
- **Other kits** of K1, K3, K4, N1 and N10 also load and check the image's `ak_l8b_fp8q.so` (R3).
- **The smoke run.** The 2 × 4 smoke of the submitted configuration on this image (800 steps) printed the same four
  first-call lines, with the same binary sha, all True, before its `run_start` (R13). The install, import and banner
  tests: [the index](../KERNELS.md#tests-before-the-scored-runs).

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12). K14's files (source, binary
`7c5815e0`, wiring module `1aca679a`) are identical in both.

- **Unit tests of the installed modules, PASS** (R4). They arm the image's own modules as `pretrain.py` does, with L4
  v2's leaf's switches, and compare every output byte with the stock path on visible, reseeded, hidden, shape-variant and
  edge cases; the installed `ak_l8b_fp8q.so` matched `7c5815e0` byte for byte. Every route passed with every check run:
  the two tests below, both again with inputs at other addresses and in an eager, capture and replay sequence, and the
  kit (leaf's switches unset, as the kits' runner runs them). All four called paths are graded (R8).
  - **Amax path** (R5): N10's quantize against TE's own (`quantize_impl.__wrapped__`), E5M2 (dO) and E4M3, on
    [s, b, 32, 128] with (s, b) = (8192, 2) as in training, (1024, 2), (1001, 1); large (×3e4), tiny (×1e-30), NaN,
    ±Inf, hidden and zero cases; and an amax making the scale exactly 32 (E4M3) or 8,192 (E5M2), which puts 524,228 and
    262,400 values on exact midpoints between FP8 neighbours (ties; R6). Graded: FP8 data, `scale_inv`, result class,
    (absent) transpose; one case replayed from a CUDA graph on new inputs. TE's defaults (power-of-2 off, epsilon 0).
  - **FP8 attention input** (R5), against TE's RoPE forward then TE's quantize: eager, K2's packed forward and K14's
    partials path (also grading the bf16 q|k|v and partial maxima); captured, K4's passes with K14's
    `scale_from_partials`, one CUDA graph replayed per case. Graded: FP8 data and `scale_inv`.
- **In-training comparison, eager runs** (R10): the stock quantize re-run on a training step's live inputs, bytes
  compared, partials (written-buffer) and amax paths: DP 8, every site every 64 steps (18 compared steps per rank),
  3,200 of 3,200 equal on each of the 8 ranks; DP 1, 512 of 512; four ranks, 64 of 64 on each rank.

### Training

K14 was on in all ten submitted runs: q|k|v took the partials path in the eager warm-up and the QKV-direct form (K4's
passes with K14's `scale_from_partials`) in every captured training and evaluation step; dO took the amax path.
